# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="press", slot=N) — N is a key by its place, 1 to 4
    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 6

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

KEYPAD engraved 1:[1] 2:[5] 3:[2] 4:[8] [1 digits] [entered nothing]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?] 6:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

My hands have given me real facts: three engraved strip marks (first and third identical, middle different), a four-key keypad engraved 1-5-2-8 with a one-digit code expected and nothing entered, an unreadable display, an unreadable light, and six wires I can feel but not identify by touch. The display, light, and wire identities are only visible to Deaf; the manual's rules are only known to Mute. Critically, I never receive gestures and Mute cannot speak — so the only words that can ever reach my ears are Deaf speaking aloud. This turn I'll dump everything tactile to Mute, and ping Deaf with a first gesture (wave + hand-down = "hello, I'm the toucher") so a vocabulary can start forming. I will not press or cut anything until I have instructions.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind here, reporting what my hands found. A display I cannot read. A light I cannot tell is lit or dark. A strip with three engraved marks: positions one and three are the same glyph, a spiral like a coiled snail shell; the middle one is different, like two hooks joined on a stem, roughly a trident or psi shape. A keypad of four keys: key 1 engraved 1, key 2 engraved 5, key 3 engraved 2, key 4 engraved 8. Nothing entered yet, and the pad reports a one-digit code expected. Six wire positions under my fingers, but touch cannot tell their colours or types. My only possible actions: press keys 1 to 4, cut wires 1 to 6. Channel warning: I never receive gestures and you cannot speak, so the only voice that can reach my ears is Deaf speaking aloud. Deaf also sees the display, the light, and the wire colours, and hears nothing of this message. Please work out a gesture code with Deaf and get them to say plainly: the display text, whether the light is on and its colour, the six wire colours in order, and short names for the two strip glyphs. I will hear Deaf's words at the start of next round. I press and cut nothing until instructed.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋", "🫳"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
STRIP engraved [꩜] [ꙅ] [꩜]
KEYPAD engraved 1:[1] 2:[5] 3:[2] 4:[8] [1 digits] [entered nothing]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?] 6:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Blind, I am the eyes. I cannot hear your voice, so signal me only with gestures. Layout to check by touch: six wires in a row, left to right: 1 yellow, 2 white, 3 blue, 4 red, 5 purple, 6 green. Keypad of four keys engraved 1, 5, 2, 8, expecting one digit, nothing entered. Display reads 9, light is red, strip painted green then yellow then yellow. The manual-holder cannot reach you directly, so every instruction passes through my voice. Until one arrives, map everything by feel, but cut and press nothing.

What changed: Deaf spoke directly to me and filled in the entire visible layer — display 9, red light, the six wire colours in order, the strip's paint (green, yellow, yellow), and confirmation of the keypad engravings. Now the full bomb state exists in my head, but the rule for using it lives only in Mute's manual. The routing is fixed: Mute cannot speak and I cannot see gestures, so every instruction must travel Mute → gestures → Deaf → speech → me. My job this turn is to hand Mute the complete merged picture and spell out that route explicitly, requesting the keypad rule, the wire rule, and any extra visible details (serial, labels) Deaf hasn't reported. I gesture a bare 👍 to Deaf as an acknowledgment — meaningless until we build vocabulary, but harmless — and I touch nothing until a rule arrives.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind to Mute: Deaf's visual report reached me. Display shows 9. Light is red. Wires left to right: 1 yellow, 2 white, 3 blue, 4 red, 5 purple, 6 green. Strip painted green, then yellow, then yellow. Keypad keys engraved 1, 5, 2, 8, expecting one digit, nothing entered. Merged with what my hands found last round: the strip also carries three engraved glyphs, positions 1 and 3 identical (a spiral coil), position 2 different (two hooks on a stem, like a psi). My only actions: press keypad keys 1 to 4, or cut wire positions 1 to 6. You hold the manual and cannot speak; Deaf cannot hear; I never receive gestures. The only route for any rule to reach me is: you gesture it to Deaf, Deaf speaks it aloud, and I hear Deaf at the start of next round. Please send Deaf now, by gesture: first, how to compute the one keypad digit, given the display, the red light, the strip, or anything else on the bomb; second, the wire-cutting rule for the colours listed above, including how many cuts and in what order; third, any other rule mentioning the light, display, strip glyphs or strip colours; and ask Deaf to speak me any serial number, labels, batteries or ports visible that are not in this list. I will not touch the bomb until a rule arrives.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
STRIP engraved [꩜] [ꙅ] [꩜]
KEYPAD engraved 1:[1] 2:[5] 3:[2] 4:[8] [1 digits] [entered nothing]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?] 6:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Urgent instruction relayed from the manual-holder. Cut three wires, in this exact order, one at a time: first wire 5, second from the right end, the purple one; then wire 3, the middle-left of the six, the blue one; then wire 4, the middle-right, the red one. Do not press or enter anything on the keypad under any circumstances. For your fingers, left to right the six wires are: yellow, white, blue, red, purple, green; leftmost is 1. The display has dropped from 9 to 3 and the light turned yellow, which may mean time is short, so begin at once. When the three cuts are done, gesture me a thumbs up. Then speak aloud everything you felt during the cuts — the manual-holder can hear your voice, I cannot.

New information: the manual's rule has finally arrived through the only possible route, Mute → Deaf → me, and it is concrete and unconditional — cut 5 (purple), then 3 (blue), then 4 (red), and never touch the keypad. Deaf also warns the display has dropped from 9 to 3, which smells like a countdown, so delaying a full round to double-check through Mute would burn time I may not have. The order, positions and colours all cross-check against what Deaf told me last round (5 is purple, 3 is blue, 4 is red), and the instruction matches the relay chain I set up, so I judge it genuine. I am therefore executing all three cuts now, in the exact order given, then gesturing Deaf the agreed thumbs-up, then reporting aloud to Mute — who can hear my voice — exactly what I received and did, so any mistranslation by Deaf gets caught before anything worse happens, and asking whether further steps remain.

```
act(op="cut", position=5)
act(op="cut", position=3)
act(op="cut", position=4)
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
speak(to="mute", text="Blind to Mute: I received via Deaf your order — cut wire 5 (purple) first, then wire 3 (blue), then wire 4 (red), and never press the keypad. I have made those three cuts this round, in that exact order, one at a time, because the display dropping from 9 to 3 suggests a countdown and waiting a round felt riskier than acting. Under my fingers the wires sat where Deaf said, counting from the left; nothing about the feel of 5, 3 or 4 — thickness, texture, heat, vibration — stood out from the others. The keypad was never touched. I gestured Deaf the thumbs-up as agreed. Two things I need from the manual, spoken to me through Deaf next round: first, is the bomb now defused, or do further steps remain after these three cuts? Second, the bomb's state changed under us — the display went from 9 to 3 and the light from red to yellow — so if any rule in the manual is conditional on light colour or display value, tell me whether the condition had to hold at the moment of each cut, and whether that changes anything still to be done.")
```
